zones.label: Alternating Saturday
zones.summary: Meets every other Saturday, all year.
facts: Low weekly time commitment for families and mentors
Works well for library and community-centre venues open at weekends
The two-week gap can weaken momentum for younger students
Predictable and easy to plan around long-term

zones.label: Weekday After-School
zones.summary: Meets weekly, right after the school day.
facts: Highest attendance consistency, since students are already at or near the venue
Competes directly with sports practices and other after-school activities
Requires mentor availability during working hours, favouring retired or flexible-schedule mentors

zones.label: Semester-Based
zones.summary: Runs for a defined term, then breaks and re-enrols.
facts: Gives a clean, low-pressure exit point for families and mentors each term
Requires a full onboarding process (Chapter 6) at the start of every new term
Well suited to a curriculum with defined tracks (Chapter 15)

zones.label: Drop-In
zones.summary: No fixed roster -- students attend whichever sessions work for them.
facts: Lowest commitment barrier for families to try the club
Hardest model to plan mentor capacity for, since attendance is unpredictable
Poor fit for mentor pairing consistency (Chapter 10)
Works best for high-traffic venues like a bookstore or library with heavy walk-in footfall
